title: Request Decomposition Time Lens: interactive trace decomposition for faster incident triage
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design an interactive 'Time Lens' view inside the Redwood Console trace explorer that decomposes a request into an aligned, zoomable timeline of spans and related artifacts (logs, metrics, KV cache hits) to reduce mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve for production regressions. The view must support correlation-ID-driven drilling, smart collapsing of repetitive spans, latency heatmap overlays, span-level cost attribution, and first-class integration with rollout canaries so engineers can quickly compare traces between model variants or capacity tiers.
goals: Surface critical path and top contributing spans within 3 clicks
Enable side-by-side comparison of two traces (e.g. canary vs baseline)
Filter and jump to spans by correlation ID, op type, service, or duration threshold
Provide quick links to related logs and GitHub PRs from span context
Estimate token/cost impact per span for quick cost triage
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to collapse noisy database retry spans so I can focus on the tail latency contributors
As an engineer, I want to compare a canary trace to the baseline to validate a rollout impact
As a PM, I want to see cost-impacting spans to prioritize optimization work
acceptance_criteria: Zoomable timeline that supports 10ms to 60s ranges and preserves span alignment
Smart-collapse toggle with grouping heuristics (by op name + service) and an expand-all option
Correlation ID search that highlights matching traces across time window and links to raw logs
Canary-Baseline diff mode showing per-span delta in latency and cost
Prototype implemented in Figma and engineering has initial API contract (trace-summary + span-stream endpoints)
Latency heatmap overlay computed from span duration distribution for the selected time window
design_notes: Key UX decisions: default to 'critical path' focus (auto-prioritize service spans with >5% tail contribution), show relative duration bars with absolute ms on hover, enable keyboard navigation for span stepping. We will place the rollout comparison as a top-level toggle in the trace header: 'Compare with: [baseline|canary|other]'. For noisy spans (e.g., short DB ops repeated 100s), use aggregated bucketed view showing count + representative span with a chevron to expand. Cost attribution will be shown as an estimated token+inference-unit cost per span; label these as estimates and link to 'Cost breakdown' panel in Console.
tradeoffs: Full-trace retrieval provides richest context but increases load on telemetry storage; initial release will rely on sampled full traces plus on-demand fetch for full span streams.
Aggressive collapsing reduces visual noise but can hide low-frequency regressions; provide 'show hidden spans' pulse and clear affordance for expanding grouped spans.
Cost estimates per span are heuristic (model-dependent) — surfaced as 'estimate' with link to Optimize recommendations for follow-up.
dependencies: ENG-32005 (logs-join-service): join logs by correlation ID
PM-412 (rollout-metadata): expose canary/baseline mapping for trace annotation
implementation_notes: Backend: add optional query params to span-stream endpoint: ?collapse=heuristic&include_cost=true&compare_to=trace_id. Frontend: virtualized timeline canvas (SVG + WebGL fallback), incremental fetch for expanded groups, keyboard next/prev span hooks. Accessibility: ensure spans expose aria-label with service/op/duration and keyboard controls for expand/collapse.
metrics: percent_traces_using_compare_mode (goal: 10% of trace sessions in month 1)

review_feedback: UX Research: add a quick usability test script for 5 engineers to validate the expand/collapse mental model
Accessibility: ensure color not the only cue for delta; include icons/badges
Engineering: provide rate limits for on-demand full span fetch to avoid DoS during incident blasts
decisions: Ship Phase 1 with sampled full traces + on-demand expanded fetch for heavy traces
Default view: Critical Path + Timeline with heatmap overlay; user can toggle full-span waterfall
Include canary comparison UI but disable auto-compare for tenants without rollout metadata
risks: High cardinality traces may trigger expensive queries — mitigated via sampling and on-demand fetch
Cost estimation may be misunderstood — always label as estimate and link to cost explainability doc
